# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.
I'll investigate the transaction labeling code and reproduce the misfiled payment cases from the incident.

# Codebase exploration: payment/transaction labeling

## Directory structure overview

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, gunicorn :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask app package deps
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API + bank dispatch (~936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific categorizer modules
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, Axis.py, SBI.py, Kotak.py, ...
        │   ├── IDBI.py, Indusind.py    # directly implicated by SEV-1 patterns
        │   └── ...
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared enrichment pipeline
            ├── AppUtil.py              # DF cleanup + string split/extract helpers
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # bank-specific regex library
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # purpose/merchant keyword regexes
            ├── CleanName.py            # cross-bank partyName normalization (~1971 lines)
            ├── Purpose.py              # subcategory + merchantType
            ├── CardCleanNames.py       # CREDIT_CARD party names
            ├── CardPurpose.py          # CREDIT_CARD purpose
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # self-transfer detection
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # salary clustering (SAVING only)
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # optional PFM buckets
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # optional display strings
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py        # separate /recurrentTransactions API
            ├── TransactionCategoryEnums.py
            └── TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**No test directory, no pytest/unittest files, no CI config.** Single git commit: `fc21c7f import codebase` (2026-07-15). No multi-commit history to bisect regressions.

---

## End-to-end pipeline

### API entry

| Route | Handler | Role |
|-------|---------|------|
| `POST /categorizeTransaction` | `categorizeTransaction()` | Main labeling pipeline |
| `POST /recurrentTransactions` | `recurrentTransactions()` | Recurrence clustering only |
| `GET /` | `home()` | Health |

**Request payload (expected fields):**
- `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`
- `transactions[]` → normalized via `pd.json_normalize` into columns including at least: `description`, `amount`, `type` (`CREDIT`/`DEBIT`), `balanceAfterTransaction`, `remark` (used heavily for cheques), often `transactionDate`
- optional `isPFMEnabled`

### Per-bank flow (same for every bank)

```
AppUtil.clean_input_df(transactions)
    → categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)
        [if CREDIT_CARD: card_clean_names → card_purpose]
    → purpose(transactions, accountType)
    → clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)
    → [if accountHolder] internal_payment(...)
    → [if SAVING] salary_detection(...)
    → [if isPFMEnabled] pfm_categorization → simple_description
→ JSON response
```

**Important:** Bank scripts assign **primary** `transactionCategory`, bank-local `partyName`, and sometimes `transactionSubcategory` / `merchantType` first. Shared `purpose` + `clean_names` refine those afterwards. Order matters for bugs.

### Core pattern inside each bank script

Every bank module follows the same structure:

1. **Category rules** – ordered `conditions_choices` list → `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`
2. Init empty `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`
3. Optional bank-local subcategory / merchant rules
4. **Payee extraction** – more `np.select` over `description`/`remark` using split/extract helpers
5. **Name cleanup** – blank bad tokens, `str.title()`, build `party2` (spaces removed)

`np.select` uses **first matching condition**, so rule order is critical.

---

## Key files and functions

### Controller / dispatch
| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | `categorizeTransaction()`, bank if/elif chain |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` | Flask app, logging, request timing |

**Supported `bank` strings:**  
`ANDHRA_BANK`, `SBI`, `ICICI`, `HDFC`, `IDFC`, `BANK_OF_INDIA`, `IDBI`, `KARNATAKA`, `UNION_BANK`, `BANK_OF_BARODA`, `PNB`, `SYNDICATE`, `KOTAK`, `CANARA`, `AXIS`, `INDUSIND`, `KARUR_VYASA`, `BANK_OF_MAHARASHTRA`, `CITY_UNION`, `UCO`, `YES`, `FEDERAL`, `RBL`, `CENTRAL_BANK`, `DCB`, `CITI`, `PAYTM_BANK`, `STANDARD_CHARTERED`, `AU_SMALL_FINANCE_BANK`, `BANDHAN`, `INDIAN_BANK`, `SOUTH_INDIAN`, `SARASWAT_BANK`, `SVC_BANK`, `TAMILNAD_MERCANTILE`

### Parsing / labeling primitives
| Path | Functions |
|------|-----------|
| `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | `clean_input_df`, `sep_by_` (`/`), `sep_by_dash` (`-`), `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_star`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_under`, brackets, `py_extract`, `fuzzy_match` |
| `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Cheque/ACH/POS/verification/charge regex constants per bank |
| `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Purpose keywords (salary, loan, shopping, bounce reasons, etc.) |

### Bank categorizer entry points
Pattern: `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)`  
Examples: `categorize_HDFC_transactions`, `categorize_IDBI_transactions`, `categorize_Indusind_transactions`, `categorize_Axis_transactions`, …

BOM/CityUnion/UCO also take `accountHolder`.

### Shared post-processing
| Function | File | What it does |
|----------|------|----------------|
| `purpose` | `Purpose.py` | Fills/overrides `transactionSubcategory`, sometimes `transactionCategory`, `merchantType` |
| `clean_names` | `CleanName.py` | Normalizes known merchants into clean `partyName`; bank-specific tweaks |
| `card_clean_names` / `card_purpose` | Card* | CREDIT_CARD path only |
| `internal_payment` | `InternalPayment.py` | Fuzzy match party vs holder → `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` + `isInternalPayment` |
| `salary_detection` | `SalaryDetection.py` | Mode/frequency salary on SAVING |
| `pfm_categorization` | `PFMCategorization.py` | High-level PFM buckets |
| `simple_description` | `SimpleDescription.py` | `pfmSimpleDescription` display |

### Output category vocabulary
`TransactionCategoryEnums.TransactionCategory` – includes `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `TRANSFER`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES`, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`, `POS_REFUND`, `REFUND`, `AUTO_PAYMENT`, etc.

---

## How raw statement text is parsed

There is **no separate statement-file parser** in this repo. Upstream already turns statement lines into rows with `description` (+ optional `remark`). This service only **regex-classifies** those strings.

Typical extraction approaches:
1. **Delimiter split** – `sep_by_(desc, i, j)` on `/`, `-`, `:`, `*`, etc.
2. **Regex capture** – `py_extract(desc, pat="...(group)...", index=N)` → `Series.str.extract`
3. **Keyword contains** – `description.str.contains(pattern)` for category labels
4. **Remark heuristics** – e.g. `remark` matching `^[0-9]{3,6}$` → cheque number only
5. **Default** – unmatched → `transactionCategory = "TRANSFER"`, `partyName = ""`

---

## Mapping the five SEV-1 bugs to code

### 1. Cheque with only cheque number → `TRANSFER` instead of cheque

**Mechanism:** Many banks only label cheques when:
- description has `CHQ`/`CLG`/`MICR`/`CHEQUE`, **or**
- `remark` is a short numeric cheque number (`^[0-9]{3,6}$` etc.)

If the **description itself** is only a cheque number (or remark is missing/empty), rules often miss and `np.select` defaults to **`TRANSFER`**.

**Representative locations:**
- `HDFC.py` L71–75, L100 – CHQ keywords; credit-only special remark; **no** generic “numeric-only description → CHEQUE”
- `HDFC.py` L124 – 6-digit description on CREDIT+SAVING even becomes **SALARY** subcategory while category stays TRANSFER
- `Axis.py` L56–59 – CLG + remark `^[0-9]{5,6}$`
- `BOB.py` L68–70 – CHQ keywords + remark digits for DEBIT
- `ICICI.py` L69–72 – CLG / remark contains `"CHEQUE"`
- `Indusind.py` L55–64 – CHQ keywords + remark `^[0-9]{5}$` for DEBIT only
- `IDBI.py` L55–58 – letters-only or `NNNNNN-` style; pure digits may not match
- `PNB.py`, `Kotak.py`, `YES.py`, `UCO.py`, `RBL.py` – similar remark-based patterns

**Fix surface:** bank-specific category blocks (and sometimes partyName when category is CHEQUE_*).

---

### 2. `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → partyName `"NACH"` instead of `"ACME INDUSTRIES"`

**Confirmed root cause in IDBI:**

```83:84:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-NACH", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
```

Dash split of `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → `['ACH','BD','NACH','ACME INDUSTRIES']`  
`sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)` → **`NACH`**. Correct slice is **`3,4`** → `ACME INDUSTRIES`.

Category is still `AUTO_PAYMENT` (L38: `\\bACH-|Direct Debit|^NACH`), so this is a **payee extraction** bug, not category.

**Related (working) patterns for comparison:**
- `HDFC.py` L169: `^ACH D- BD-NACH-` → `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` (correct offset for that format)
- `Axis.py` L134: `^NACH-DR- BD-` → `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)`

---

### 3. `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` → blank partyName

**Confirmed root cause in IDBI:**

```110:110:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}", na=False, case=False) , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)],
```

- Condition matches (`GBHDL` + 10 digits).
- Capture group is only index **0**, but code uses **`index=1`**.
- `py_extract` (`AppUtil.py` L61–66): if `.get(index)` is `None`, returns empty Series → **blank name**.

Verified: extract with `index=0` yields `RAVI KUMAR`; `index=1` yields `None`.

---

### 4. Token confirmation / mandate charges → ordinary `TRANSFER`

**Verification path:** `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` only if amount is ~1/-1 **and** description matches bank verification regexes (`BANK_VER`, `BANK_VER_ICICI`, `ACC_VERIF`, etc. in `BankRegexConstants.py`).

**Mandate charges path:** `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` only on bank-specific keywords, e.g.:
- Axis/Indusind: `MNDTVRFCHGS`
- SBI: `^ACH MANDATE CHARGE|E mandate|\\bACH\\b CHARGE?`
- Kotak: `^MANDCHAR|Chrg.*ECS|...`
- IDBI: only `"E mandate"`
- HDFC: soft token fees folded into general `CHARGES` via `BANK_CHARGES_HDFC` (`AMC SOFT TOKEN`), not verification

Narratives like bare **“TOKEN CONFIRMATION”**, generic mandate setup, or Rs≠1 verification pennies that lack those keywords fall through to **`default="TRANSFER"`**.

Also note Axis L26: **any CREDIT of amount 1** → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` (aggressive); other banks are stricter.

**Secondary:** `Purpose.py` L165 can re-label LOAN subcategory amounts 1/-1 as `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` category.

---

### 5. Card refund → plain `REFUND` instead of card reversal (account-type dependent)

**Confirmed bug in Indusind:**

```26:27:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py
        [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bPOS TXN",na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.amount.ge(10) & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL"],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bPOS TXN",na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVING") , "REFUND"],
```

- Codebase uses **`SAVING`** (singular) everywhere else in Controller.
- First rule checks **`SAVINGS`** (plural) → **never matches**.
- Second rule matches **`SAVING`** → always **`REFUND`**.

So savings POS credits become plain refund, not `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`.

**Similar account-sensitive logic:**
- `BankOfMaharashtra.py` L31–32: amount > 10 → reversal, else refund for `\bPOS TXN`
- `HDFC.py` L20–21: `^CRV POS|^POS REF` with amount < 25 → `REFUND`, else `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`
- ICICI/Canara/BOB/etc. have their own POS reverse patterns

---

## Test files

**None found.** No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `pytest.ini`, tox, or Makefile test targets.

### How to run / exercise the service

```bash
# Install (as Dockerfile does)
cd /app/categorizationapp
pip3 install -e .

# Dev server
python -m categorizationapp   # or: flask / python categorizationapp/__init__.py → :9898

# Production-style
gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app

# Docker
docker build -t categorizationapp /app
# EXPOSE 9898
```

**Manual regression probe** (no harness exists):

```bash
curl -s localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "bank": "IDBI",
  "acc_type": "SAVING",
  "accountUID": "u1",
  "accountHolder": "",
  "transactions": [{
    "description": "ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES",
    "amount": 500,
    "type": "DEBIT",
    "balanceAfterTransaction": 1000,
    "remark": ""
  }]
}'
```

Repeat for other banks/narratives. Unit tests would call `categorize_*_transactions` + `purpose` + `clean_names` on DataFrames directly.

---

## Recent changes / regression history

| Finding | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| Git history | **Single commit** `import codebase` — no prior diffs to attribute regressions |
| mtime oddity | Most files stamped Nov 2 2022; **IDBI.py** and **Indusind.py** also show Jul 15 2026 touch in listing — both are SEV-1 hotspots |
| No changelog / PR trail | Cannot prove a recent edit caused the bugs; several look like long-standing off-by-one / typo issues |

Highest-confidence defect sites for this SEV-1:
1. **`IDBI.py` L83–84** – ACH-BD-NACH dash index  
2. **`IDBI.py` L110** – `py_extract` index `1` vs `0` for `GBHDL…`  
3. **`Indusind.py` L26–27** – `SAVINGS` vs `SAVING` for card reversal  
4. Cross-bank cheque remark/description gaps → default `TRANSFER`  
5. Incomplete verification/mandate keyword coverage → default `TRANSFER`

---

## Architecture summary (mental model)

```
Statement text (upstream)
        │
        ▼
JSON {description, remark, amount, type, ...}
        │
        ▼
BankScripts.categorize_*  ──► transactionCategory (np.select, default TRANSFER)
                          ──► partyName (delimiter/regex extract)
                          ──► optional subcategory/merchant/city
        │
        ▼
Purpose.purpose           ──► refine subcategory/merchant; sometimes category
        │
        ▼
CleanName.clean_names     ──► normalize merchant display names
        │
        ▼
internal_payment / salary_detection / PFM (optional)
        │
        ▼
JSON response rows
```

**Primary fields produced:** `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2`, sometimes `city`, `isInternalPayment`, `pfmCategory`, `pfmSimpleDescription`.

---

## Practical fix entry points (for the SEV-1 work)

| Bug | First file to edit | Function / lines |
|-----|--------------------|------------------|
| ACH-BD-NACH name | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` | partyName block ~L83–84 (`sep_by_dash` indices) |
| GBHDL name blank | same `IDBI.py` | ~L110 (`py_extract` → `index=0`) |
| Cheque number only | each affected bank’s category block; shared patterns in `BankRegexConstants.py` | `remark`/`description` numeric rules before default TRANSFER |
| Token/mandate | bank category blocks + `BankRegexConstants` verification/mandate regexes | `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` / `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` rules |
| Card refund | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py` | L26–27 (`SAVINGS`→`SAVING`); review BOM/HDFC amount gates |

Recommend adding a **pytest suite** under e.g. `categorizationapp/tests/` calling bank categorizer functions with the five narrations (no tests exist today to prevent recurrence).
